APPELLATE AUTHORITY  REPRESENTED BY THE COMMISSIONER AND SECRETARY TO THE GOVT.
 OF ASSAM  HOME AND POLITICAL DEPT.
 DISPUR-781006  9:ADDL. SECRETARY TO THE GOVT. OF ASSAM  HOME AND POLITICAL DEPARTMENT  DISPUR-78100
Advocate for the Petitioner : MR. M K DAS, A BHARADWAJ,C SAIKIA,S J DUTTA
Advocate for the Respondent : GA, ASSAM, SC, AG,SC, FINANCE
BEFORE  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ANJAN MONI KALITA  ORDER Date : 08.08.2025 Heard Mr. M. K. Das, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Also heard Mr. J.K.
Goswami, learned Additional Senior Government Advocate for the respondent Nos. 1,3,4,5,6,8 & 9 and Mr. R. Borpujari, learned counsel for the respondent No.2.

None appears for the respondent No.7.
2.

The case of the petitioner is that while he was serving as the Superintendent of Police in the District of Darrang, an F.I.R was lodged by one Sri Kamal Krishna Baruah, before Dhula Police Station and the UD case was registered.
Subsequently, an F.I.R was also lodged by one Shri Raju Turi, father Page No.# 3/4 of a minor girl alleging rape and murder of his minor daughter.
Accordingly, Dhula P.S. Case No. 114/2022, was registered under Sections 376/302 of IPC, POCSO Act, and Child Labour Act.
Accordingly, the investigation was made into the matter and the accused person was arrested and sent to the judicial custody.
3. It is being informed to the Court that a trial regarding that offence is still going on.
While the petitioner was serving a show cause notice dated 06.12.2022, was issued to him with charges based on three statement of allegations.

A perusal of the show cause notice shows that the petitioner has been alleged to her committed serious supervisory lapses and misconduct unbecoming of a Raj Mohan Ray vs The State Of Assam And 8 Ors on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2319325/
2 responsible APS Officer holding the post of Superintendent of Police and thereby he has committed gross negligence of duty and serious lapses in supervision of a serious case of alleged rape and murder of a minor girl and misconduct.

sentences.text: The petitioner was also provided with the list of documents and list of witnesses which were to be relied upon by the authorities.
The petitioner has submitted a reply to the show cause notice on 19.01.2024.
He participated in the proceeding and thereafter, an enquiry report along with affording letter dated 26.09.2023, was submitted by the respondent authorities.

From the enquiry report, it transpires that allegation No.1 is proved and allegation Nos.
2 & 3 are partially provided.

4. After the completion of departmental enquiry by the orders of the Governor dated 01.04.2024,
the petitioner was dismissed from service with immediate affect against the dismissal order dated 01.04.2024.

The petitioner has preferred an appeal under Section 15 of Assam Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1964 against by impugned order of punishment dated 01.04.2024, which has also been rejected by the Appellate Authority i.e. the Page No.# 4/4 Governor vide its order dated 27.03.2025.
5.

Aggrieved by such order of his dismissal the petitioner has preferred this writ petition with a prayer to set aside and quashed the aforesaid dismissal order contending that there are serious lapses on behalf of the respondent authorities in conducting the departmental enquiry process.
He submits that additional witnesses have been called for though those witnesses were not named in the list of witnesses that has been provided to the petitioner.

6. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the counsel for the respondents and of the view that, at this stage, notice should be served on the respondent authorities for proper adjudication of the matter.
Since, Mr. J.K. Goswami, learned Additional Senior Government Advocate is appearing in the matter for respondent Nos. 1,3,4,5,6,8 & 9 notices on those respondents are dispensed with.
Mr. R. Borpjuari appears for respondent No.2, therefore notice may not be issued for respondent No.2.
Notices may be issued by registered post with A/D to respondent No.7, returnable within 4 (four) weeks.
7. The petitioner to take steps of service of notice within 3 (three) days.
The petitioner is also directed to serve the requisite nos. of extra copies to the respondents.
8. Let the matter be fixed after 4 (four) weeks.
